correctness.rationale: For every unit pair, signed norming facets for the two symmetric chords convert the weighted chord expression into two dual-functional norms. Exact evaluation over the ten signed facets gives the sharp bound \(A+rB\le3-r\), and sign reversal gives its symmetric companion. These inequalities and \(0\le A,B\le2\) define a six-vertex outer polygon for every feasible chord pair. The quadratic inequality equivalent to the desired P-angle bound is convex, so its maximum on that polygon is attained at a vertex; exact evaluation gives maximum four. The adjacent-vertex pair has chord norms \(2\) and \(r\), attaining the claimed value.
risks: The argument requires the signed facet list to be exhaustive; the checker verifies the ten primal vertices and ten dual facets exactly.
The source preprint states a standing dimension restriction in its preliminaries; only its displayed P-angle definition is used here in dimension two.

value.rationale: The result is not only an isolated radical evaluation. The sharp inequalities \(A+rB\le3-r\) and \(rA+B\le3-r\) give a structural outer description of all symmetric chord pairs in a canonical non-Hilbert decagonal plane, and the P-angle value follows from a convex quadratic optimization on that envelope. This adds a natural exact benchmark to existing hexagonal, octagonal, dodecagonal, and classical-sequence-space computations and exposes the golden-ratio support mechanism specific to the decagon.
risks: The structural envelope is specific to the decagon; no general regular-polygon law is claimed.
